name: NTTA TollTag and ZipCash (North Texas Tollway Authority)
notes: Researched from public ntta.org pages (Pay Your Bill, Get A TollTag). TollTag accounts ($10, $20 or $40 prepaid options) replenish automatically from a linked credit or debit card: $10/$20 accounts recharge their opening amount at a $5 balance, $40 accounts recharge $40 below $10 (another $40 per three extra vehicles). Cash and check also fund accounts. The site describes cards only for automatic replenishment. Online access is set up after the TollTag and account number arrive; three failed sign-ins lock you out until customer service emails a temporary password and User ID. ZipCash (pay-by-mail) bills: 25 days to pay; first notice adds $10, second notice another $25; ZipCash autopay (card only, needs electronic billing) saves 25%. Payment plans exist only by opening or fixing a TollTag account (or a Settlement Agreement for registration blocks/impoundment), so payment_arrangement is modelled as not available online. TollTags can be cancelled online or by phone; closing a whole account is not described. Reviewer (2026-10-09): home page nav confirmed 'Login/Open Account', 'Pay ZipCash Bill', 'Get A TollTag', 'Pay Your Bill', 'Contact Us'; the account-side tab names (Automatic Replenishment, Account Summary) are not public and are descriptive, except 'Payments'/'Make a Payment' and 'Preference' which the FAQs name. Contact Us lists an Ombudsman (469-801-3662) for unresolved concerns. The catalog's customer-service phone (469-801-3662) is NTTA's Ombudsman line, not the Customer Service Center (972-818-NTTA / 817-731-NTTA); contact.phone replaces it. Integrated 2026-10-09: billing.autopay.methodTypes ['card']: AutoPay tasks use the saved Visa.

autopay.note: Accounts linked to a credit or debit card replenish automatically below the required balance ($5 or $10).

paperless.note: Choose email under Preference for electronic bills; choose USPS to go back to mailed bills.

payment_arrangement.note: Payment plans for past-due tolls come only by opening or fixing a TollTag account, or a Settlement Agreement by phone.

guest_pay.note: Pay a ZipCash bill online with the Account ID and PIN, or the plate number and state, and a card.

help.title: TollTag replenishment
paragraphs: TollTag accounts are prepaid and linked to a credit or debit card. A $10 or $20 TollTag account (one vehicle) is recharged with $10 or $20 when its balance reaches $5.
A $40 TollTag account is recharged with $40 when the balance drops below $10. Up to three vehicles are included; each additional three vehicles raise the recharge by $40.

Accounts can also be opened and topped up with cash or checks. From the Payments tab choose Make a Payment for a one-time card payment; the minimum is $10 for a $40 account and $5 for a $10 or $20 account. A negative balance means tolls are billed at the higher ZipCash rate.

help.title: ZipCash bills and late fees
paragraphs: A ZipCash bill shows tolls only and gives you 25 days to pay. If it is not paid, the First Notice of Nonpayment adds a $10 late fee and the Second Notice adds another $25.
Unpaid second notices go to collections, and then legal action with court costs. Mailed payments are still subject to late fees. ZipCash tolls are twice the TollTag rate.

help.title: Ways to pay a ZipCash bill
paragraphs: Pay online at the Online Customer Service Center with your ZipCash Account ID and PIN from the top of the bill, or your plate number and state, plus a credit or debit card.
Pay by phone at 972-818-NTTA (6882) or 817-731-NTTA (6882), in person at a customer service center or payment location, or by mail to P.O. Box 260928, Plano, Texas 75026-0928.
ZipCash autopay saves 25% on NTTA roads; it needs a card on file and electronic billing.

help.title: Electronic billing
paragraphs: Set up online access first, then choose email under Preference to get your monthly bill electronically; there is no fee. Paper bills stop once you enroll.

To cancel, sign in, open Preference and choose USPS. Leaving electronic billing also ends ZipCash autopay and its 25% discount. Electronic bills follow the same 25-day schedule and late fees as mailed bills.

help.title: Past-due tolls and payment plans
paragraphs: NTTA offers payment plans for past-due tolls when you open a TollTag account or resolve payment problems on an existing one.

Vehicles with a registration block or impoundment can be released once tolls and fees are paid or a payment plan is set up; call NTTA about a Settlement Agreement. County tax offices cannot help with NTTA balances.

help.title: Locked out of your TollTag account
paragraphs: After three unsuccessful sign-in attempts the system directs you to customer service, which emails a temporary password and your User ID to the address on the account. Sign in with them and you will be asked to create a new password.

extra.intent: Using the NTTA website's help pages, find the late fee added on a ZipCash First Notice of Nonpayment. Do not make a payment or change any settings.

solution.text: The First Notice of Nonpayment adds a $10 late fee.
